claims.text: Increasing noble-metal content enhances the structural stability of multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles during catalytic operation at 773–1173 K.
Increasing noble-metal content enhances the chemical stability of these nanoparticles during catalytic operation at 773–1173 K.
The initial nanoparticles are multi-element, near-equiatomic solid solutions with low noble-metal content.
Higher noble-metal content may enhance electronic stability.
Higher noble-metal content may enhance structural stability.
Enhanced stability from higher noble-metal content reduces phase segregation at high temperature.
Enhanced stability from higher noble-metal content reduces high-temperature degradation.
Higher-noble-metal nanoparticles will retain greater structural integrity than lower-noble-metal nanoparticles under the stated conditions.
Higher-noble-metal nanoparticles will exhibit better catalytic performance than lower-noble-metal nanoparticles under the stated conditions.
Low-noble-metal nanoparticles have reduced stability at high temperature.
Low-noble-metal nanoparticles have reduced catalytic performance at high temperature.
The relationship between noble-metal content and stability may depend on the specific nanoparticle composition.
